_comment: Media Protection Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with PE (PE-16 delivery / removal is the gating workflow for MP-5 transport), MA (MA-3(2) media inspection echoes MP scanning practice; MA-2 sanitization-before-maintenance overlaps MP-6), SC (MP-4 / MP-5 cryptographic protection of stored / transported media uses SC-12 / SC-28 keys), and SI (SI-12 information management overlaps MP-6 / MP-7 lifecycle). Compact family — 7 base controls and no enhancements at moderate; the rigor is in classification-driven handling and sanitization evidence.
title: Media Protection Plan
description: Documents how the system's storage media — both digital and non-digital — are governed across access, marking, storage, transport, sanitization, and use. Covers the controls of the MP family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-88 r1 (Sanitization Guidelines), CNSSI 1253 (Categorization and Control Selection for National Security Systems), 32 CFR Part 2002 (CUI Marking), and FIPS 199 / FIPS 200 categorization frameworks.
intro_template:
This Media Protection Plan documents the media-protection approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, tooling, cadences, and roles used to control access to system media, mark media according to classification and handling requirements, store media in protected locations, transport media outside controlled areas, sanitize media before reuse or disposal, and govern the use of removable and portable media.

The scope covers media access per MP-2, media marking per MP-3, media storage per MP-4, media transport per MP-5, media sanitization per MP-6, and media use per MP-7 within the {system_name} authorization boundary. Both digital media (drives, tapes, removable media) and non-digital media (printed reports, written notes containing CUI) are in scope where applicable. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Media Protection family), NIST SP 800-88 r1 (Sanitization Guidelines), and 32 CFR Part 2002 (CUI Marking).
approach_template:
{system_name} tracks media through {media_inventory_system} with the role responsibilities documented in §3 (Roles and Responsibilities). Sanitization is performed by {sanitization_service} per NIST SP 800-88 r1, with destruction certificates retained at {destruction_certificate_storage}. Media transport outside controlled areas follows {transport_custody_workflow}. Removable media use is governed by {removable_media_policy_summary}.

Additional details on media access, marking, storage, transport, sanitization, and use are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Media-protection performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (media-inventory currency rate, sanitization-certificate completeness, MP-5 transport SLA compliance, removable-media policy violations, marking-audit findings, lost / unaccounted media count). Media inventory is reconciled on the cadence in §6.2; lost-media incidents (target: zero) feed the IR plan workflow. Sanitization certificates are audited annually for completeness against the corresponding decommission events.
integration_template: This Media Protection Plan does not stand alone. The PE family supplies the PE-16 delivery / removal workflow that gates MP-5 transport; the MA family inspects media via MA-3(2) and sanitizes via MA-2 before vendor maintenance, both echoing MP-6; the SC family supplies the cryptographic protection (SC-28) and key management (SC-12) underwriting MP-4 / MP-5 protection of media at rest and in transit; the SI family's SI-12 information-lifecycle management overlaps with MP-6 / MP-7. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where MP-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Tooling and roles that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: Media inventory system (one-liner)
questions.help: Where storage media are inventoried (e.g., 'CMDB media-asset module', 'Dedicated media-tracker spreadsheet under version control', 'Inherited from cloud — no system-managed physical media').

questions.label: Sanitization service / vendor
questions.help: Who performs media sanitization (e.g., 'Internal IT Operations using Blancco Drive Eraser', 'NSA-listed vendor for Purge / Destroy', 'GSA-schedule contract destruction vendor').

questions.label: Destruction-certificate storage location
questions.help: Where certificates of destruction are retained (records-management system, GRC tool, secure file share).

questions.label: Transport chain-of-custody workflow
questions.help: Brief phrase summarizing transport workflow (e.g., 'GSA-bonded courier with sealed tamper-evident container; chain-of-custody form per shipment', 'Encrypted transport via FedEx with signature-required tracking + post-transit verification').

questions.label: Removable-media policy summary (one-liner)

family_questions.label: Media Inventory
family_questions.description: Categories of media in scope and how they are tracked.

questions.label: Digital media categories
options: Internal hard drives (HDD / SSD) in servers / workstations / laptops
Cloud-provider object / block storage (logical, but governance applies)

questions.label: Media-inventory reconciliation cadence
questions.help: How often the media inventory is reconciled with physical reality (e.g., 'Quarterly with annual full audit').

family_questions.label: Media Access (MP-2)
family_questions.description: Who can access media and on what basis.

questions.label: Authorization criteria
questions.help: What entitles a person to access controlled media (need-to-know, role-based, screening level — reference PS-3).

questions.label: Access-logging requirement
questions.help: When access events to controlled media are logged. Sign-in / sign-out for physical media; system audit for digital media access (overlaps with AU-2).

questions.label: Authorization-list review cadence
questions.help: How often the authorized-access list is reviewed (typical: 'Annually + on personnel change'). MP-2 ODV.

questions.label: Marking systems in use
options: CUI marking per 32 CFR Part 2002 (CUI Basic / Specified)
Classified marking per ISOO (Confidential / Secret / Top Secret)
PII / PHI / PCI / FTI handling labels

questions.label: Marking method by media type
questions.help: How each media type is marked. Example: 'Backup tapes: serialized adhesive label with classification + asset tag; portable drives: laser-engraved housing + register entry; hardcopy: top-and-bottom-of-each-page banner per 32 CFR Part 2002.'

questions.label: Marking exemptions (MP-3 ODV)
questions.help: Per MP-3 ODV, types of media exempted from marking requirements (e.g., 'Public-information media in a controlled facility'). Document rationale.

questions.label: Marking-audit cadence
questions.help: How often the marking is audited (e.g., 'Quarterly random sample of media items'). Captures markings degraded by wear or improperly applied at issue.

family_questions.label: Media Storage (MP-4)
family_questions.description: Where and how media at rest is physically protected.

questions.label: Storage location types
options: Locked room with PIV / CAC access
Tape library with encryption + access control
Cloud-provider managed storage (logical, but inventory tracked)

questions.label: Cryptographic protection of stored media (MP-4)
questions.help: How stored media is cryptographically protected. SED + LUKS + BitLocker / FileVault for portable media. Reference SC-12 / SC-28 for keys + at-rest encryption.

questions.label: Environmental protection
questions.help: Temperature, humidity, EMI / magnetic-field protection where applicable (especially for tape archives). Reference PE-14 for facility environmental.

questions.label: Off-site media-storage arrangement
questions.help: If applicable: off-site provider name, contract, access-control posture, audit cadence. Reference SA-9.

family_questions.label: Media Transport (MP-5)
family_questions.description: Movement of media outside controlled areas.

questions.label: Transport scenarios in scope
options: Laptop + external drive transport for telework

questions.label: Chain-of-custody requirements
options: Signed COC form retained per shipment

questions.label: Authorized couriers (MP-5 ODV)
questions.help: Couriers authorized to transport media outside controlled areas. Cleared employees, GSA-bonded carriers, vendor-cleared personnel. MP-5 ODV.

questions.label: Transport-encryption requirement
options: Mandatory for all media leaving facility (FIPS 140-3 validated)
Mandatory for CUI / classified; exempt for public
Mandatory for digital media; physical sealing for non-digital

family_questions.label: Media Sanitization (MP-6)
family_questions.description: Sanitization methods, certificates, and decision criteria.

questions.label: Sanitization categories applied (NIST SP 800-88 r1)
options: Clear (logical erasure — overwrite or factory reset)
Purge (cryptographic erase, degauss for magnetic, NVMe sanitize, ATA secure-erase)
Per data classification — Clear for Low; Purge for Moderate; Destroy for High / Classified

questions.label: Sanitization-decision matrix
questions.help: How the sanitization category is chosen. Reference NIST SP 800-88 r1 Decision Tree (Reuse vs Recycle, Internal vs External, Sensitivity).

questions.label: Sanitization-validation requirement
questions.help: How sanitization is validated. Tooling logs (Blancco / Killdisk certificate), random-sample re-read tests, vendor-provided certificate of destruction with serial-number match.

questions.label: Destruction techniques per media type
questions.help: How each media type is physically destroyed when destroy is required (e.g., 'HDDs: degauss + shred; SSDs: cryptographic erase + shred; tapes: shred; optical: shred').

questions.label: Witness requirement
options: Documented but not actively witnessed (vendor self-attestation)

questions.label: Sanitization-process review cadence
questions.help: How often the sanitization process / equipment is reviewed for effectiveness. MP-6 ODV.

family_questions.label: Media Use (MP-7)
family_questions.description: Restrictions on removable and portable media use.

questions.label: Authorized media types

questions.label: Enforcement mechanism
questions.help: How media-use policy is enforced (DLP, GPO, MDM port restrictions, physical port blockers, BIOS password).

questions.label: Exception process
questions.help: Workflow for granting exceptions to media-use policy (e.g., for vendor-supplied installation media). Time-limited exception with retroactive review.

questions.label: Media-origin restriction (MP-7)
questions.help: Per MP-7 ODV, restriction on media without identifiable owner (anonymous origin). Common posture: prohibited for non-public information.

glossary.definition: Documented sequence of transfers of an asset from one custodian to another, supporting accountability and forensic admissibility. Required by MP-5 for media transport.
Per NIST SP 800-88 r1, sanitization category that uses logical techniques (overwrite, factory reset) appropriate when the media will be reused within the same organizational sensitivity context.

Per NIST SP 800-88 r1 Purge category, sanitization by destroying the cryptographic keys protecting encrypted data, leaving the data unrecoverable. Particularly effective for SED drives and self-encrypted storage.
Controlled Unclassified Information — federal information requiring safeguarding controls per 32 CFR Part 2002 / EO 13556. Drives MP-3 marking and MP-4 / MP-5 / MP-6 protection requirements.
Per NIST SP 800-88 r1 Purge category, sanitization of magnetic media by exposure to a strong magnetic field that randomizes the media's magnetic alignment. Not applicable to SSDs.
Per NIST SP 800-88 r1, sanitization category that physically destroys the media to a state where data recovery is infeasible (shred, incinerate, pulverize). Required for high-sensitivity disposal.
Federal Information Processing Standard validating cryptographic modules. MP-4 / MP-5 cryptographic protection of media uses FIPS-validated modules per agency policy.
Group Policy Object — Windows mechanism for centrally enforcing endpoint configuration, including USB-port restrictions for MP-7 enforcement.
Mobile Device Management — platform enforcing policy on mobile devices and laptops, including media-port restrictions and remote-wipe capability for MP-6(8).
Per MP family, media that does not store data in digital form: printed reports, handwritten notes, hardcopy. Subject to marking (MP-3) and sanitization (typically shredding for MP-6).
NIST Special Publication 800-88 Revision 1 — Guidelines for Media Sanitization. The authoritative reference for MP-6 sanitization category selection.

Per NIST SP 800-88 r1, sanitization category appropriate when the media will be reused outside the original sensitivity context. Techniques include cryptographic erase, degauss for magnetic, ATA Secure Erase / NVMe Sanitize for solid-state.
Media designed for portability (USB drives, optical disks, removable hard drives, memory cards). Subject to MP-4 storage and MP-5 transport, plus MP-7 use restrictions.
Per MP-6, the process of removing data from media to prevent recovery. Categorized as Clear, Purge, or Destroy per NIST SP 800-88 r1.
Self-Encrypting Drive — storage device with built-in hardware encryption. Allows efficient cryptographic erase by destroying the embedded encryption key.
Packaging that displays visible evidence if opened. Required by MP-5 chain-of-custody for sensitive transport.
Per MP-6, a second qualified person observing and attesting to media destruction. Required for high-sensitivity destruction events.
